verses.text: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
Casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?

Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’ For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things. But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul.
Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we won’t be afraid, though the earth changes, though the mountains are shaken into the heart of the seas.
“Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted amongst the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”
In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, the LORD, make me live in safety.

The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
The LORD is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? The LORD is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
I sought the LORD, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him. He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I will never be greatly shaken.
I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth. He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber.
Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
But now the LORD who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.”
For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused.

“Come to me, all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm. He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height? If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.
For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
The LORD himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.
The LORD, your God, is amongst you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
It is because of the LORD’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his mercies don’t fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
Return to your rest, my soul, for the LORD has dealt bountifully with you.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.
But those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
Love your own soul, and comfort your heart. Remove sorrow far from you, for sorrow has destroyed many, and there is no profit in it.
He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”
The LORD’s angel encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

messages.text: Breathe in slowly and pray, Jesus. Breathe out and pray, I trust in You.
You do not have to solve tomorrow today. God is already there.
Cast all your anxieties on Him, because He cares for you. All of them, even the small ones.
Jesus calmed the storm with a word. He can calm the storm inside you.
Worry tells you the worst will happen. Faith reminds you that God is with you whatever happens.
Name what you are worried about, then hand each worry to God, one by one.
Be still, and know that He is God. Even one minute of stillness helps.
The birds do not worry about tomorrow, and your Father feeds them. You are worth more than many birds.
Anxiety is not a sin. It is a burden. Let Jesus help you carry it.
Saint Padre Pio said, Pray, hope and do not worry. Try it for one hour today.
God's peace is not the absence of problems. It is His presence in the middle of them.
When your thoughts race, slow your body: unclench your hands, relax your shoulders, breathe.
Martha was anxious about many things. Jesus invited her to sit at His feet. He invites you too.
You are held by a God who never sleeps. You can rest.
Pray the Rosary slowly. Its gentle rhythm can quiet an anxious heart.
Fear not is written in the Bible again and again. God knew you would need to hear it.
If anxiety is overwhelming, talking to a doctor or counsellor is wise, and it is not a lack of faith.
Take the next small step. God will light the one after that.
God has not given you a spirit of fear, but of power, love and self-control.
Mary, Our Lady of Peace, pray for us. Rest in her motherly care.
Write your worries down, then pray over the list and place it before God.
The Lord fights for you. You only need to be still.
You cannot add one hour to your life by worrying, but you can add peace by praying.
Thank God for three things right now. Gratitude loosens the grip of worry.
Do not fear, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
Whatever happens, you will not face it alone.
Seek first the kingdom of God, and let Him take care of the rest.
When you lie down tonight, say: In peace I will lie down and sleep, for You alone make me safe.
Try a short prayer whenever worry rises: Jesus, You take care of it.
The future belongs to God, and God belongs to you. Trust Him with it.
Peace I leave with you, Jesus said. It is His gift. Receive it.
Step outside, look at the sky and remember how big God is.
Anxiety often lives in the future. God meets you in the present moment.
Do what you can today, and offer the rest to God.
Saint Francis de Sales taught: Do not look forward to what might happen tomorrow. The same Father who cares for you today will care for you tomorrow.
God holds the whole world, and He holds you.
Your heart can rest in God like a child resting in its mother's arms.
You are not your anxious thoughts. You are a beloved child of God.
Ask a friend to pray with you. Worry shrinks when it is shared.
Let God carry tonight's worries while you sleep. He will be awake.
When everything feels uncertain, hold on to what is certain: God's love for you.
Prayer does not always change the situation at once, but it always changes the heart.
Turn off the news and the phone for a while, and let your mind rest in God.
Christ is in the boat with you. The storm cannot sink it.
Fear knocked at the door. Faith answered, and no one was there.
Breathe in God's peace, breathe out your fear. Repeat as often as you need.
The God who cared for you yesterday will not abandon you tomorrow.
You can be anxious and still trust God. Bring both to Him honestly.
Today has enough to deal with. Leave tomorrow in God's hands.
Rest now. The Lord is your shepherd; you shall not want.
